findings.finding: AC3 requires 'the delta against the epic's prediction', but the packet defines `delta_kib` as before minus after and stores the band separately. No field computes the measured after-size against the band. The band is also in MiB while the measurements are in KiB (365–380 MiB = 373,760–389,120 KiB), and the band is hardcoded.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add to the fixture at least one event signed by a test key (expected verified), placed on each side of the boundary, and assert non-zero `verified` counts before and after.
evidence: "with identical before and after counts (7 unsigned events)"
"The reclaim must not change any event's verdict."
findings.finding: The happy-path fixture appears to contain only unsigned events ('7 unsigned events'). The before/after verify-identity comparison therefore cannot detect the main risk: a history rewrite that changes a verified event's verdict, or makes an era-dependent verdict (key-not-valid-at-era) drift because the commit position or date changed.
findings.location: Testing → Happy path (`identity_counts_equal: true ... (7 unsigned events)`)
scenarios: The collapse rewrites commits so that era resolution for a signed event changes. With an all-unsigned fixture the counts stay {unsigned: 7} and the test passes.
findings.suggested_fix: Generate a throwaway signing key in tmp_path and sign one CREATE before the horizon and one COMMENT after it. Assert that identity_before.counts == identity_after.counts and that counts['verified'] == 2.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Compare per-event verdicts (event id → verdict) before and after where verify-identity can emit them, or explicitly state that count equality is an accepted proxy.
evidence: "The same enforced `verify-identity --all` must report the same per-verdict counts as before. The reclaim must not change any event's verdict."
findings.finding: The plan states that the reclaim must not change ANY event's verdict, but the check compares only aggregate per-verdict counts. Offsetting changes would pass, and an event that moves in or out of scope is not identified.
scenarios: One event goes verified→unsigned while another goes unsigned→verified, and the counts stay equal.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert that every after-state ledger `position.commit_sha` exists in a fresh clone of the fake remote and is an ancestor of the new tip, and record the result (e.g. `ledger_shas_on_branch`) in the packet.
evidence: "ignoring each authorship-ledger `position.commit_sha`. The reclaim re-resolves those values onto the rewritten commits by design"
findings.finding: Reducer equality ignores `position.commit_sha`, but nothing verifies that the re-resolved SHAs actually point at commits on the rewritten branch. A dangling or stale (pre-reclaim) SHA would pass.
scenarios: The ledger keeps an old T0-era SHA that is reachable only via refs/tickets-backup. The reduced state matches and the check passes, but a fresh clone cannot resolve the SHA.
findings.suggested_fix: For each after-state ledger entry, run `git merge-base --is-ancestor <commit_sha> <new_tip>` in a fresh clone of the fake remote. Fail the run on any miss and include the count in evidence.json.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Snapshot the source's full `git for-each-ref` output (and optionally `git config --list --local`) before and after the run. Record `source_refs_unchanged` from a full-set comparison, and assert it in the happy-path and failure-path tests.
evidence: "`source_ref_unchanged`, from re-resolving `--ref` in the source"
AC1: "never writes to the source; `tests/unit/test_reclaim_dry_run.py` asserts `source_ref_unchanged`"
findings.finding: 'Never writes to the source' is proved only by re-resolving the single `--ref` in the source. A bug that pushed or updated a different source ref would go undetected. Examples: publish aimed at the source URL instead of the fake remote, or a stray update-ref against the wrong repo. The same applies to config changes or a new refs/tickets-backup/* ref in the source.
scenarios: A misdirected publish creates refs/tickets-backup/* or a new refs/heads/tickets in the source; `--ref` (e.g. origin/tickets) still resolves the same, so `source_ref_unchanged: true` is reported.
The real run against a developer checkout silently mutates a branch other than origin/tickets while the packet says the source is untouched.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture `git -C <source> for-each-ref --format='%(refname) %(objectname)'` before step 1 and after step 7. Store both digests in evidence.json. Fail the run and report the diff if they differ.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Set the horizon anchor ref as `refs/remotes/{config.tickets_remote(shadow)}/{config.tickets_branch(shadow)}` (and name the branch the same way), or state that the harness pins these config values for the shadow.

A user-layer `sync.remote` or `tracker.branch` override on the developer workstation would make S1 look for a different ref than the one the harness set.

findings.suggested_fix: Resolve remote = config.tickets_remote(shadow) and branch = config.tickets_branch(shadow) after the shadow exists, then run `git update-ref refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch> T0`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the no-grandfathering premise hold regardless of config: pass an explicit empty `--since` (or another override that clears enforce_since) together with `--require-authenticated`, or check that the composed `identity.enforce_since` is unset before running.

src/rebar/_config_schema.py:201-210: enforce_since is a config key; REBAR_IDENTITY_ENFORCE_SINCE is just its env override

A project or user config that sets identity.enforce_since would still grandfather events and change the recorded exit codes.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace or extend `source_ref_unchanged` with a full `git for-each-ref` snapshot (refs and SHAs) of the source taken before and after the run, record the diff in evidence.json, and say how a concurrent update to the source's remote-tracking ref is told apart from a harness write (e.g. run the real pass against a quiescent `git clone --mirror` source, or check that T0 still resolves rather than requiring the ref to stay put).
evidence: Plan: "`source_ref_unchanged`, from re-resolving `--ref` in the source"
Plan AC: "never writes to the source; ... asserts `source_ref_unchanged`"
Plan [non-codebase] AC: "run once against a read-only fetch of the real `origin/tickets`" on a developer workstation
findings.finding: `source_ref_unchanged` is the plan's only evidence that the harness 'never writes to the source', and it is both too weak and too fragile. It is weak because re-resolving one ref says nothing about other refs, config, or objects. When `--ref` is a raw SHA it is always true. It is fragile because the [non-codebase] AC runs it against `origin/tickets` in a developer's live checkout. A background `rebar sync` or fetch there can move `origin/tickets` during a long real-scale run, so the harness fails even though it wrote nothing.
findings.location: Approach step 8 (`source_ref_unchanged`); Acceptance Criteria 1 and [non-codebase] AC
scenarios: Real-scale run takes minutes; the workstation's sync updates refs/remotes/origin/tickets in the source, so the packet reports source_ref_unchanged:false and exits non-zero.
A future change makes the harness write a different ref (e.g. refs/heads/fetched) into the source, and source_ref_unchanged still passes.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] After the rewrite, add a third enforced `verify-identity --all` run with `REBAR_IDENTITY_ENFORCE_SINCE=<result.enforce_since>`. Record its enforced versus grandfathered counts in evidence.json, and check that the enforced set equals the events introduced at or after the ledger anchor (in the synthetic test, the replayed unsigned events are enforced and the below-boundary ones are grandfathered).
evidence: Plan: "no `REBAR_IDENTITY_ENFORCE_SINCE`, so every event is checked and none is grandfathered"
Plan: "`result.enforce_since` must be an ancestor of the new tip ... This guards the defect fixed by `euhedral-svelte-chimpanzee`"

Ticket a67d-5760 (euhedral): "`verify_authorship._is_enforced` ... enforces an event only when `git merge-base --is-ancestor <since_ref> <event commit>` succeeds ... every event in the rewritten history is grandfathered"; its own regression test ran verify-identity with REBAR_IDENTITY_ENFORCE_SINCE=<enforce_since>
findings.finding: The identity comparison runs only with no `REBAR_IDENTITY_ENFORCE_SINCE`, so every event is enforced. That is not how the gate will run after the swap, when the grandfather boundary is the re-anchored `result.enforce_since`. The euhedral-svelte-chimpanzee defect showed up exactly in that mode: an anchor that does not sit on the branch grandfathers every event. The plan covers it only indirectly, with a `merge-base --is-ancestor` check that is close to automatic on the shadow, because the stamp commit is made on top of the collapsed tip. The packet never shows that the post-swap gate enforces the replayed events and grandfathers only the collapsed ones.
findings.location: Approach steps 5 and 7 (verify-identity runs; enforce_since ancestry check)
scenarios: A regression makes events replayed above the anchor look like ancestors of enforce_since, or makes _is_enforced resolve a different commit. The ancestry check still passes, yet the post-swap gate grandfathers events it should enforce.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make step 5's 'none is grandfathered' hold no matter which config file is loaded (for example run with `--format json` and assert no report entry has `grandfathered: true`, or run from a cwd with no project config), and record the effective enforce_since in the packet.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py:431-436: `cfg = config.compose_config(root=args.root)` ... `since_ref = args.since if args.since is not None else cfg.identity.enforce_since`.

findings.finding: Step 5 claims that running verify-identity with 'no REBAR_IDENTITY_ENFORCE_SINCE' means 'every event is checked and none is grandfathered'. verify-identity reads `cfg.identity.enforce_since` from compose_config(root=args.root), meaning the cwd checkout's and user's config layers, whenever the env var and --since are absent. Leaving the env var unset does not clear a config-file enforce_since. Verdict counts are computed either way, but the recorded exit codes and the 'none grandfathered' guarantee depend on the operator's config.

scenarios: The real run is launched from a rebar checkout whose project config sets identity.enforce_since. Pre-anchor events are then grandfathered, and exit codes in identity_before/identity_after differ from what the plan describes.

Fail the harness if any entry has grandfathered=true. Set the subprocess cwd to <workdir> so no project-level config layer applies.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the fixture's events (type, signed or unsigned, commit date relative to the horizon) so the expected per-verdict counts follow from the fixture definition.

"(7 unsigned events)"

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that the after reducer and identity checks run on a fresh non-bare clone of the fake remote checked out at the new tip, not on the shadow.

Step 7 names no target repository for the reducer or identity re-run.

Checking the shadow does not prove what was published. If collapse moves the ref without updating the worktree, REBAR_TRACKER_DIR=<shadow> may read stale files.
scenarios: The publish pushes a tip that differs from the shadow's state, but the after-checks run on the shadow and pass.
findings.suggested_fix: After the publish, run `git clone --no-local --branch tickets file://<fake-remote> <workdir>/after`. Run reduce_shadow_tracker and `verify-identity --all` with REBAR_TRACKER_DIR=<workdir>/after.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the exact arguments passed to collapse_shadow_tracker (boundary commit and/or horizon), state that the cutoff uses committer date relative to a single captured `now`, and record `now`/`cutoff` in evidence.json.

"`collapse_shadow_tracker(..., apply=True)`"

scenarios: The harness reports one boundary while S1 collapses at a different one computed internally from event timestamps.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the structured output (or exact parse rule) used for the verdict counts, fail if any expected verdict key is missing, and define the stored output tail (e.g. the last 50 lines).
evidence: "the per-verdict counts (...) printed by an enforced `python -m rebar verify-identity --all`"
"the last part of its output"

scenarios: A wording change in verify-identity's summary breaks the parser, or makes both sides parse to {}, which compares equal.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether the reclaim adds events. If it does, define how they are excluded from or accounted for in the count comparison and the reducer equality.
evidence: "then `stamp_superseding_epoch`"
"must report the same per-verdict counts as before"

scenarios: The stamp writes an unsigned epoch event, so the after-count reads unsigned: 8 against 7 before, and the harness reports a false failure.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Run all git and rebar steps under a scrubbed environment: unset REBAR_* except the explicitly set ones, disable the S3 adapter, and set GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM and core.hooksPath. Assert this in a test.

AC5: "publishes only to a file:// fake remote inside that workdir"

On a developer workstation, REBAR_* variables (including any S2 S3-bundle adapter settings), REBAR_TRACKER_DIR, or global git config (hooks, commit.gpgsign, remote insteadOf rewrites) could make in-process collapse/publish calls reach real storage or behave differently from the test.
scenarios: S3 bundle variables are set in the operator's shell, publish_git_ref uploads a bundle of the rewritten history to the real bucket, and a dry run causes a real side effect.
A global commit.gpgsign=true signs the rewritten commits with the operator's key or blocks on pinentry.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define commit counts as `git rev-list --count <T0>` and `git rev-list --count <new_tip>` in the fake remote, and durations as seconds (float) keyed by step name.

"per-step durations"
findings.finding: Commit counts and per-step durations have no stated computation: which revisions or ranges, first-parent or all, and in what units.
scenarios: One implementation reports first-parent counts and another reports all commits, and humans compare packets across runs.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether the predicted band includes the `.retired` sweep, and record a `prediction_assumptions` note in evidence.json.
evidence: "The `.retired` sweep (`mystical-capsizable-ibis`) is paused ... so it is not part of this run."

scenarios: The human sees pack_kib_after above the band and reads it as a reclaim failure rather than a scope difference.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a short doc (e.g. a module docstring rendered in the reclaim runbook, or an ADR 0106 addendum) describing the invocation and every evidence.json field.

findings.finding: The plan adds a new operator-facing CLI and a machine-readable evidence.json contract that a human consumes, but names no doc, runbook entry, or schema description for either.
scenarios: The human reviewing the go/no-go has to read source code to learn what each packet field means.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether `stamp_superseding_epoch` adds an event or reducer-visible state. If it does, define the expected delta explicitly (e.g. after = before + exactly one epoch event with verdict X) instead of strict equality, and assert that delta in the test.
evidence: "`collapse_shadow_tracker(..., apply=True)` ... then `stamp_superseding_epoch`, then `publish_git_ref`"
"The same enforced `verify-identity --all` must report the same per-verdict counts as before"
"identical before and after counts (7 unsigned events)"
findings.finding: The plan runs `stamp_superseding_epoch` between the before and after measurements, then requires identical per-verdict counts (the test pins '7 unsigned events') and an equal reduced state. It never says whether the stamp writes an event or reducer-visible state that `verify-identity --all` or `reduce_shadow_tracker` would count. If it does, the oracle is wrong by construction, or the implementer will quietly exclude the stamp to make it pass.
scenarios: The epoch stamp is recorded as a new event. The after count becomes 8 unsigned (or 7 unsigned + 1 verified), and the happy path goes red or gets patched with an undocumented exclusion.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a short failure-disposition contract for the harness: mark check-failure arms as fatal/NO-GO and harness or environment errors as retryable (re-run in a fresh workdir). Say how the publish CAS rejection is classified. Encode the class in evidence.json (e.g. `error_kind: check_failed|harness_error`), with distinct exit codes.
evidence: "The command exits non-zero if any check fails, and writes the packet with an `error` field before it exits."
"`publish_git_ref` to `file://<fake-remote>` with `expected_old_tip=T0`"
findings.finding: The harness adds a failure exit ('non-zero ... packet with an `error` field') but states no disposition per failure arm. Three outcomes need distinguishing: (a) a reclaim-correctness check failed, which means NO-GO; (b) a harness or environment error such as a git subprocess failure, disk full, or verify-identity crash, which is transient and safe to retry; (c) a CAS rejection from `publish_git_ref` (`expected_old_tip=T0`) on the fake remote. The packet gives the human no way to tell them apart, and the plan does not say what state a mid-run failure leaves in the workdir.
findings.location: Approach step 8 ("The command exits non-zero if any check fails") and step 6 (publish with expected_old_tip)
scenarios: A transient git failure during the after-clone produces the same non-zero exit and `error` shape as an identity-count mismatch. The human reads it as a reclaim defect (false NO-GO), or reads a real mismatch as flakiness.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR=<shadow>` and the identity env vars are set only in the child `python -m rebar verify-identity` subprocess env, never in the harness's own `os.environ`, and add a test assertion for this.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_collapse.py:180-191: live = config.tracker_dir(None).resolve(); if live == tracker: raise ShadowSafetyError; ConfigError/OSError -> ShadowSafetyError('cannot resolve live configured tracker')
src/rebar/_config_sources.py:103: os.environ.get('REBAR_TRACKER_DIR')
findings.finding: Every S1/S2 entry point runs `_assert_shadow_tracker`. That guard resolves `config.tracker_dir(None)` and rejects the target if it equals the live tracker or if the live tracker cannot be resolved. If the harness sets `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR=<shadow>` in its own process environment (step 5 says only 'runs with REBAR_TRACKER_DIR=<shadow>'), the collapse, stamp and publish will refuse with 'refusing to rewrite live configured tracker'.
scenarios: The implementer sets os.environ['REBAR_TRACKER_DIR'] before running verify-identity in-process, and the later collapse raises ShadowSafetyError.
findings.suggested_fix: Run verify-identity via subprocess.run([...], env={**os.environ, 'REBAR_TRACKER_DIR': shadow, 'REBAR_IDENTITY_REQUIRE_AUTHENTICATED': '1'} minus REBAR_IDENTITY_ENFORCE_SINCE), and keep the parent process env unchanged.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `rebar fsck` and a full-log replay/rebuild of the rewritten shadow to step 7, record `fsck_clean` and `replay_equal` in evidence.json, and assert both in the happy-path test (or update the parent epic to drop them from the staging gate first).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State and check the capability step 1 relies on: either force protocol v2 for the T0 fetch (`git -c protocol.version=2 fetch ...`) and add a test where `--ref` names a non-branch ref, or fetch the ref by name (`+<ref>:refs/heads/fetched`) and then assert the fetched tip equals the resolved T0.
evidence: Plan: "`git fetch --no-tags <source> <commit>:refs/heads/fetched`, where `<commit>` is `--ref` resolved in the source ... lets the real run read `origin/tickets`"

Retrieved: git Documentation/config/uploadpack.adoc (chromium mirror) — "uploadpack.allowReachableSHA1InWant:: Allow `upload-pack` to accept a fetch request that asks for an object that is reachable from any ref tip ... Defaults to `false`."
Retrieved: isaacs/github#436 — the reachable-SHA1-in-want flag "is off by default".
findings.finding: Step 1 fetches a bare commit SHA (`git fetch --no-tags <source> <commit>:refs/heads/fetched`) from the source. When `--ref` is `origin/tickets`, that commit is the tip of a remote-tracking ref, which upload-pack may not advertise. Retrieved git docs say `uploadpack.allowReachableSHA1InWant` defaults to false. Whether the fetch works therefore depends on transport and protocol version (it is generally expected to work under protocol v2, not under v0), and the plan neither states nor checks this.
scenarios: On a workstation with `protocol.version=0` configured, or an older git, the T0 fetch fails with 'not our ref' or 'Server does not allow request for unadvertised object', and the non-codebase AC run cannot even start.
findings.suggested_fix: Fetch by refname and then verify: `git fetch --no-tags <source> +<fully-qualified --ref>:refs/heads/fetched`, then fail if `rev-parse refs/heads/fetched` != the T0 resolved in the source. Add a unit test where `--ref` is `refs/remotes/origin/tickets` in the synthetic source.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State and enforce the fetch-by-SHA precondition in step 1 (for example `git -c protocol.version=2 fetch ...`, or fetch the resolved full refname when --ref names a ref), and add a test that fetches a non-tip commit.
evidence: Plan: 'Then `git fetch --no-tags <source> <commit>:refs/heads/fetched`, where `<commit>` is `--ref` resolved in the source.'
No git version or protocol precondition appears anywhere in the plan; Portability says only 'core git and local file:// remotes'.
Evidence class: Partially-verified. The fetch-by-SHA surface exists, but whether it is accepted depends on protocol and upload-pack config that the plan does not pin or probe.
findings.finding: Step 1 fetches a raw commit SHA (`git fetch --no-tags <source> <commit>:refs/heads/fetched`). Git upload-pack accepts a non-tip SHA as a want only under protocol v2 or when uploadpack.allowReachableSHA1InWant / allowAnySHA1InWant is set. Protocol v0/v1 rejects it with 'not our ref'. The plan relies on this without naming the precondition. A source or global config with protocol.version=0, or an older git, breaks step 1 of the real run, and the tests will not catch it on a default-config CI box.
scenarios: An operator workstation with protocol.version=0 in ~/.gitconfig runs the real dry run, and step 1 dies with 'upload-pack: not our ref'.
--ref resolves to a commit that is no longer a ref tip in the source.
findings.suggested_fix: Run step 1's fetch as `git -c protocol.version=2 fetch --no-tags <source> <sha>:refs/heads/fetched`. For a local-path source, the -c config is passed to the spawned upload-pack through GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS without writing to the source. When --ref resolves to a full refname (git rev-parse --symbolic-full-name), fetch that refname instead and then verify the fetched tip equals T0.
